elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not be required to pay Vendor any liquidated damages ... under this Agreement"
"any liquidated damages or penalty under this Agreement"

elements.element: Prior Customer-payable liquidated amount (15% of annual Fees per week) no longer operative
elements.evidence: "including any amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid" is now within the negation

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee or 3-month cap appears in the redlined clause

elements.element: Such fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: Clause states a blanket prohibition, not a sole permitted liquidated amount

reasons: The single replacement flips the Customer-payable liquidated damages obligation into an express prohibition, satisfying the preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.
Scope wording "under this Agreement" tracks the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages anywhere) rather than adding an unrelated new right, so it is not treated as excess.

Residual trigger and 15% language survive only as illustrative content inside the negation; awkward but harmless, with no dangling obligation and Vendor's other Section 7 remedies (e.g., interest/suspension) untouched.
Fallback is not satisfied and need not be, since the drafter's locked target is the preferred level.
